correctness.rationale: For three additive agents, known horizon m>=6 and each frequency multiset {H,1^(m-1)}, with H>(m-2)(m-3), the policy maintains nonempty completion by forced fill when remaining goods equal empty bundles. Before first shared-high arrival, only at most one unsatisfied agent is occupied; the shared-high good has an empty high recipient, who is frozen. Later distinct high values are allocated to owners or forced-fill singletons. Thus any high good assigned to a nonowner is in a singleton, and otherwise own value>=1 whereas deleting a unit from any other bundle leaves at most m-3 low goods. Gives 1/(m-3)-EFX. Adaptive adversary first delivers m-2 all-low goods and makes penultimate high for early recipients P, final high for complement. An exhaustive final-two-recipient case analysis bounds every realized allocation by max((m-2)/H,1/(m-3)), with the assumed H threshold giving matching equality. Independent game recursion for m=6,H=13 yielded exact 1/3 with 1964 cached states, and source code covers more horizons; quantifier proof is analytic.
